newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Slovakia may join OECD this year - Johnston.
newsitem.headline: Slovakia may join OECD this year - Johnston.

text.p: Slovakia may become a member of the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) this year but further rapid expansion of the organisation is less likely, the OECD said on Monday.

Secretary General Donald J. Johnston told a news conference that among countries who wished to join the OECD, Slovakia was the closest to membership, adding that the organisation was unlikely to expand further rapidly after Slovakia's admission.
"I would not foresee a rapid expansion in the foreseeable future," he told a news conference.
The OECD signed a cooperation pact with Russia one month ago, without giving a firm date to Moscow for joining the organisation.

Johnston told Reuters he had been optimistic that Slovakia could join the OECD in 1996, however the talks with Slovakia about privatisation issues, financial markets and other questions were still going on in the OECD's committees.
Slovakia's final qualification "is a political judgment made by the members based upon the recommendation of the committees", he said.

He declined to predict a specific date for Slovakia's joining the OECD but he said he hoped it would take place in the relatively near future. When aske whether a 1997 date was likely, he said: "It is always possible,"
